_note: Job type templates. The pipeline matches a Jobber job title against `match` keywords (lowercase, any hit wins, longest match preferred) and renders the JOB PREP panel from the winning entry. `buy` is the Home Depot or supplier run. `tools` is gear beyond the EDC bag. `site` is sequence and gotchas. Subtract anything already in jobs/edc.json before rendering.

types.label: Shower door replacement
buy: The door unit, measured against the opening before leaving the house
100% silicone, clear, mildew resistant, 2 tubes
Wall anchors rated for the frame, plus plastic shims
Carbide or diamond bit if anchoring into tile
Silicone remover and fresh razor scraper blades
Isopropyl for the track bed
Contractor bags rated for glass
tools: Hacksaw or angle grinder for cutting track to width
Cut resistant gloves and safety glasses
Cardboard or moving blanket to protect the pan
site: Photo the old door before demo, that is the before shot
Dry fit the track and check level before a single hole gets drilled
Silicone cures 24 hours, tell the client in person that the shower is out until tomorrow morning
Haul away means a dump run, check the hours before promising an end time

types.label: Patio floor coating and resurface
buy: Coating and anti-slip additive, enough for the measured square footage plus 15 percent
Concrete degreaser and etcher
Crack filler and patch compound
Painter's tape and masking film for walls and posts
Roller covers rated for the coating, plus spare
Respirator cartridges if the product calls for them
tools: Pressure washer with surface cleaner attachment
Grinder with a cup wheel for any high spots
Moisture meter or a plastic sheet for the tape test
site: Run the moisture test the day before, a slab that reads wet kills the whole job
Watch the radar. Coating plus a Florida afternoon storm is a redo
Two day job on the calendar means day one is prep and day two is coat, do not compress it
Tell the client the cure window and when furniture can come back

types.label: Flooring removal and install
buy: Planks plus 10 percent waste, same lot number
Underlayment if the spec calls for it
Transition strips and quarter round
Fresh utility blades and a spare oscillating blade
Leveling compound for any dips
tools: Oscillating multi tool for door jambs
Shop vac and a long straightedge
site: Acclimate the planks in the room, check the manufacturer window
Check subfloor flat before anything gets laid
Undercut the jambs, do not scribe the plank
Haul away the old floor same day, it takes more truck space than it looks

types.label: Cabinet and interior install
buy: Cabinet screws, not drywall screws
Shims and filler strips
Touch up marker matched to the finish
Hardware and jig if pulls are in scope
tools: Stud finder and a long level
Drill and impact with a full bit set
Track saw or circular saw with a guide for scribing
site: Find and mark every stud before the first cabinet goes up
Set the high point of the floor first, everything references off it
Photo inside the wall before it closes up

types.label: Door replacement
buy: The slab or prehung unit, hinge hand confirmed
Shims, low expansion foam, exterior caulk
Weatherstrip and threshold if exterior
Lockset and strike plate with 3 inch screws
tools: Router with hinge template if mortising fresh
site: Confirm the swing and hand with the client before demo, not after
Never leave an exterior opening unsecured at end of day
Foam sets slow, plan the lockset install around it

types.label: Yard detail. Hedge, edge, anchor
buy: Fast setting concrete, one bag, for the bird bath base
Landscape spikes or rebar pins for the edging line
Contractor bags and a tarp for the hedge clippings
Fresh string for the trimmer head
Blade lube and a can of resin remover for the hedge shears
tools: Hedge trimmer plus a hand shear for the tight spots
Level and a rubber mallet for setting the bath
Flat shovel and a hand tamper
Wheelbarrow or a bin for hauling clippings
site: Photo the hedge line and the bird bath before anything moves, that is the before shot
Set the bird bath level and plumb before the concrete grabs, you get one shot
Edge first, then trim, then blow everything down last so you clean once
Clippings ride out with you, do not leave a pile at the curb unless the client asked
Florida afternoon storms roll in after 11, get the concrete set in the morning
